Encounter a conditional branch, splitting the flow into taken and not-taken arms.
Advance the taken arm through its specific instruction sequence.
Affirm the successful execution of the taken path logic.
Advance the not-taken arm, potentially reversing direction or jumping to a target.
Evaluate the negative path, checking for decode failures or invalid targets.
Rejoin the taken and not-taken arms at the common successor point.
Continue the linear chain after the branch rejoin.
Encounter a second branch or a function pointer dispatch.
Traverse the primary execution path of the second branch.
Detect an early return or exit in one arm, holding the open fork state.
Attempt to fuse the arms, resulting in a B state due to the open fork.
The system reads its own compiled image, establishing self-reference.
Chain the self-referential state back into the main audit flow.
Fix the audit record, permanently storing the verdict and surplus count.
